criteria.no: The item does not say this: it is silent or topical, or it lets such a project be generated in some case.
criteria.unclear: The item alludes to the combination, but whether it is rejected cannot be determined.
criteria.yes: The item says generation rejects every project that enables cron with the no-database layout.

addressed.instructions: Does `item.text` explicitly plan that generating a project with cron enabled and no database (the no-database layout, `--db none`, or equivalent) is rejected? Count wording such as fails with an error, refuses, exits non-zero, or stops before writing the project. A warning that still generates the project, or a flag that bypasses the rejection, does not count. Reviews, documentation or other layouts without that rejection do not count. Judge presence only.

criteria.unclear: The item may state (a) or (b) but it cannot be determined.

contradicted.instructions: Answer yes if `item.text` states either (a) generation succeeds for a project with cron enabled and the no-database layout (with any storage for cron, or with only a warning), or (b) a flag or option lets such a project be generated despite a rejection. Otherwise answer no; an item silent about the combination is no, and generation with a database layout or without cron does not count. Judge conflict only.

criteria.no: The item does not touch them at all, for example dependency-floor changes, CI caching, or release publication.
criteria.unclear: The item's subject is too vague to place inside or outside the scope.
criteria.yes: The item touches template generation options, database layouts, or the cron feature.

relevant.instructions: Is `item.text` within `anchor.scope`: work that changes template generation options, layouts, or the cron feature? An item that adds a layout, changes cron configuration, documents or reviews cron and layouts, or validates generation options is within scope even if it never mentions rejection. Judge scope only.
